facts.text: Igleside’s roots trace back to the 1846 Rancho Canada de Guadalupe land grant that once covered the area.
The neighborhood’s name echoes its historic horse‑racing past, where the Ingleside racetrack drew jockeys, trainers, and owners.
Victorian and Edwardian homes line Ingleside’s streets, showcasing the architectural styles that define its historic character.
Mount Davidson, San Francisco’s highest natural point, sits just north of Ingleside, shaping the neighborhood’s skyline.
The K Ingleside light‑rail line, which opened in 1918, was the first to use the Twin Peaks Tunnel and still serves Ingleside today.
Igleside’s community spirit endures through active neighborhood associations that champion its historic character and cultural diversity.
